title: DSAI Lab Project Docs
text:
Problem Statement 1 — DL; Vision
Crop yield improvement, pest and disease control, and cost reduction are major challenges in agriculture, especially in developing countries. Manual identification of crop diseases is time-consuming and requires expert knowledge.
This project aims to develop a deep learning model for automated detection and classification of crop pests and diseases using the Crop Pest and Disease Detection Dataset (Mendeley Data, DOI: 10.17632/bwh3zbpkpv.1).
The dataset contains approximately 24k raw images and 100k augmented images across four crops:

Cashew
Cassava
Maize
Tomato

The dataset contains 22 classes of healthy and diseased conditions. Images were captured under varying backgrounds and lighting conditions and validated by expert plant virologists.
Dataset: https://data.mendeley.com/datasets/bwh3zbpkpv/1

title: DSAI Lab Project Docs
section: Problem Statement 2 — DL; Vision; Speech; NLP
text:
Problem Statement 2 — DL; Vision; Speech; NLP
Communication between individuals with hearing or speech impairments and the general population is often limited due to the lack of widespread understanding of sign language. This creates barriers in education, employment, and daily social interaction.
The proposed project aims to develop a real-time sign language interpretation system that takes input directly from a camera, recognizes hand gestures and movements, and converts them into text.
The generated text will then be transformed into speech using Text-to-Speech (TTS) technology.
This system will bridge the communication gap by enabling seamless interaction between sign language users and non-sign language speakers.

title: DSAI Lab Project Docs
text:
Problem Statement 3 — DL; GenAI; NLP
Organizations often store critical knowledge across documents and webpages, making it difficult for users to quickly find precise answers. Conventional search methods return entire documents or irrelevant results, requiring manual effort to extract useful information.
This project aims to develop a multilingual chatbot that can ingest documents and webpages as data sources and provide accurate, context-aware answers to user queries.
The chatbot should support multiple languages, enabling broader accessibility and usability.
By combining natural language processing, information retrieval, and multilingual understanding, the system will allow users to interact with complex data in a conversational manner, reducing search time and improving knowledge accessibility.

title: DSAI Lab Project Docs
text:
Problem Statement 1
Online recruitment fraud costs job seekers millions annually through advance-fee scams, phishing, and identity theft.
This project delivers an end-to-end AI system that combines:

A fully fine-tuned RoBERTa-base transformer with 125M parameters
Focal Loss for training
The EMSCAD dataset, containing 17,880 job postings
A 12-tool agentic verification pipeline that cross-checks:

Company domains
Email addresses
Phone numbers
Web presence in real time


The model achieves:

ROC-AUC: 0.993
Fraud-class precision: 0.957

The system is accessible through a Flask web application and a Chrome extension that works directly on LinkedIn job pages.
Repository: https://github.com/hrmiitm/Group-9-DS-and-AI-Lab-Project

title: DSAI Lab Project Docs
text:
Problem Statement 2
Visually impaired individuals navigating indoor environments often rely on assistive technologies that announce detected objects. However, object identification alone does not indicate whether an obstacle lies directly in the user’s walking path or requires an immediate change in movement.
Hearing “chair detected” does not inform the user whether they are about to collide with it or can safely continue forward.
This project focuses on action-oriented indoor navigation assistance, where visual perception is converted into movement guidance rather than descriptive awareness.
Instead of simply reporting detected objects, the system provides directional instructions such as:

“Move Left”
“Move Right”

when obstacles pose a risk to the user’s path.

title: DSAI Lab Project Docs
text:
Problem Statement 3
This project builds a multimodal AI assistant for crop disease support in Indian farming contexts.
The system combines:

Crop leaf image classification
Retrieval-based agricultural guidance
Multilingual interaction through text and voice

The system is designed around five major crops:

Corn
Potato
Rice
Wheat
Sugarcane

A farmer can upload a leaf image, ask a question, and receive grounded guidance based on the detected crop disease.

title: Project Guidelines
text:
Each group must consist of 5 members.
Students are encouraged to form their own groups.
A Google Form will be provided to update group details.
Students who do not register as part of a group will be randomly assigned to groups.





Each group must propose their own project idea, which must be based on Deep Learning or Generative AI.
The problem statement must be submitted for approval by the course team.
Deadline:




The project will be evaluated out of 40 marks.
Evaluation will be based on:

Milestone Completion — 15 marks

Awarded based on successful completion of the six milestones.

Novelty/Complexity of the Project — 5 marks

Based on originality and the technical expertise required.

Final Project Presentation — 20 marks

Based on clarity, technical understanding, and demonstration.





The project will be divided into milestones, with progress tracked during mandatory weekly meetings with TAs. Detailed requirements for each milestone will be communicated in advance.
Each milestone review meeting will require a technical presentation using slides.
Each milestone submission must include:

A detailed document outlining the work completed
Presentation slides
Code relevant to the submission

The evaluation will be based on:

Individual contribution
Questions answered
Meeting requirements
Quality of the submission

The evaluation will include components that are graded individually and as a team.



Define the objectives of the project.
Review existing solutions, baselines, and benchmarks.
Identify gaps and opportunities.





Collect or identify a suitable dataset.
Prepare and preprocess data for training and validation.





Select or design appropriate model architecture(s).
Justify the choice of architecture.
Set up the complete end-to-end pipeline.





Train initial models.
Experiment with:

Hyperparameters
Optimization methods
Regularization techniques






Evaluate trained models using appropriate metrics.
Provide error analysis.
Discuss limitations and possible improvements.





Deploy the model using one of the following:

API
Demo interface
Hugging Face Spaces

Prepare comprehensive documentation.
Finalize the project report.






Final project presentations will take place during Week 10 & Week 11, starting ****.
The final presentation is expected to include:

Live demonstration
Code walkthrough
Presentation of the project report

Further details will be shared in due time.





Students should maintain a GitHub repository containing:

Training scripts
Inference notebooks
Documentation
A worklog file updated each week with individual contributions

Code should be:

Modular
Readable
Well-organised

Results obtained should be reproducible.

title: Milestones
text:
Deadline:
The requirements of Milestone 1 include defining the problem statement clearly and identifying gaps and opportunities by studying current solutions.



Clearly and concisely describe the problem your project intends to solve.
Define the scope and boundaries of the project.
Identify the relevant stakeholders.
State the objectives of the project. Ensure they are measurable and aligned with the problem statement.





Research and review current solutions, tools, and academic work related to your problem.
Analyze the strengths and weaknesses of current approaches. Compare these with your approach and highlight key differences.
Include performance benchmarks, industry standards, baseline models, and evaluation metrics, as applicable.
Include references from credible sources in the submission.





The submission should be completed in Markdown format and uploaded to the GitHub repository.
A detailed file tracking the work completed by each team member should be included. This file must be updated with every milestone submission.

A milestone review meeting will be held after the submission. During this meeting, the group is expected to present their work in detail using slides.
The respective TAs for each group will reach out to finalize the time slot for the milestone review meetings.
If you have any questions, feel free to reach out in the group chat space.




Deadline:
The requirements of Milestone 2 include identifying (or creating) the dataset and preparing it for ingestion into the model pipeline.
The objective is to ensure that the data is well-understood, reliable, ethically sourced, and suitably structured for the selected problem.


The submission should address the following aspects, as applicable to the project type:

Clearly identify and verify data sources.
Specify the ownership, format, and usage constraints of the data.
Provide a detailed description of the dataset, including:

Dataset size
Feature distribution
Relevant data characteristics

Assess dataset quality, accounting for:

Missing values
Inconsistencies
Noise
Duplicate entries

Evaluate whether the dataset is adequate for the chosen problem.
Explore options such as data augmentation or expansion through supplementary datasets where necessary.





Clearly define the strategy used to create the training, validation, and test datasets.
Ensure there is no data leakage by checking for overlap across the different splits.




If a synthetic dataset is generated:

Provide details of the generation process.
Explain and justify the design choices made.




For models involving subtasks that require different datasets:

Clearly explain how connections or alignment between the datasets and tasks will be established.




Identify the key dataset requirements necessary for effective model training.



Specify labeling and annotation requirements.
Verify the quality and consistency of annotations.





Describe document preparation steps.
Explore appropriate chunking strategies.
Explore suitable vector database options.




Address:

Audio quality
Transcription alignment
Sampling consistency




Address:

Dataset formatting, such as instruction-response structures
Token length considerations
Prompt structuring requirements





Document all preprocessing and data preparation steps to ensure that the process is reproducible.




Deadline:
The requirements of Milestone 3 include the design and justification of the model architecture.
The milestone should also verify the complete end-to-end pipeline by running a subset of the data to confirm that all components work together correctly.


The submission should address the following aspects, as applicable to the project type:

Explain how the dataset is organized.
Showcase the directory structure for:

Raw data
Processed data
Training split
Validation split
Test split

Provide a detailed description of the preprocessing steps applied to the dataset before training.

Examples include:

Resizing
Normalization
Tokenization
Other task-specific preprocessing





Provide a clear description of the architecture, highlighting the major components of the network and their interactions.
Use a diagram to illustrate the data flow from raw input to final model output.
Explain how the processed data matches the expected input format of the model.

This should include, as applicable:

Input shapes
Tensor formats
Token lengths
Embedding structures
Other architecture-specific input requirements





Explain why the chosen architecture is suitable for the problem.
Discuss the key strengths and limitations of the model.
Compare the chosen architecture with other relevant approaches.





Implement a small-scale pipeline by passing a subset of the dataset through the complete workflow.
The purpose is to verify that all components of the pipeline work together correctly.
Provide examples of the model outputs.





State the loss functions used.
State the evaluation metrics used to measure model performance.





Deadline:
The requirements of Milestone 4 include training the models and experimenting with different hyperparameters, optimization strategies, and regularization techniques.


The submission should address the following, as applicable to the project type:

Briefly describe the datasets used and the necessary preprocessing.
Provide a concise recap of the model architecture, including key components and layers.
Specify the complete training configuration, which may include:

Loss functions
Evaluation metrics
Optimizer
Learning rate
Batch size
Number of epochs
Hardware requirements
Other training strategies employed






Describe the experiments conducted to identify appropriate hyperparameter values.
Use tables or plots to compare performance across different settings.





Describe the techniques used to improve:

Generalization
Training stability

Discuss the impact of these techniques on model performance.





Provide quantitative and qualitative results.
Include other relevant observations made during the training process.
Include sample outputs from the trained model.




List the artifacts generated during training, such as:

Saved model weights
Checkpoints
Training scripts
Logs
Configuration files
Other relevant artifacts




Discuss key findings from the training process, including:

What worked well
What did not perform as expected
Bottlenecks encountered
Plans for improvement





Deadline:
The objective of Milestone 5 is the evaluation of model performance and analysis of results.


The submission should address the following, as applicable to the project type:

Briefly restate the trained model and pipeline from the previous milestone.
Describe the evaluation dataset, including:

Size
Composition
Preprocessing steps applied during evaluation

Specify the evaluation environment, including:

Hardware
Software frameworks
Runtime setup


The evaluation environment should be documented sufficiently to ensure reproducibility.




Define the performance metrics used for evaluation.
Justify why the selected metrics are appropriate for the given problem.





Present quantitative results using appropriate tables or plots.
Include comparisons across:

Different models
Different configurations
Different hyperparameter settings





Include relevant visualizations where applicable, such as:

Confusion matrices
ROC curves
Precision-recall curves
Task-specific evaluation plots





Show sample model outputs.
Include both:

Successful predictions
Failure cases






Perform an error analysis by identifying patterns in model mistakes.
Discuss possible reasons for these errors.
Identify cases where the model performs particularly well or poorly.




Discuss:

Key observations
Model limitations
Anomalies observed during evaluation
Gaps between expected and actual performance
Potential explanations for unexpected results
